site.title: Hardly Funny
site.tagline: A webcomic about being married to a computer programmer
site.author: Samantha Degges
site.about_html:
Hardly Funny is an autobiographical webcomic that was created in 2012.

Randall and Samantha (myself) are opposites who married in 2010 and have since suffered frustrating moments of disagreement that teeter on our different outlooks. Randall is a self-taught hacker who worked from home as a lead developer while I drew these comics, and claims to be nearly perfectly organized, obsessively ambitious, and logical. (His own writing lives at rdegges.com.) Compared to that, I consider myself traditionally “normal”. I’m also witty and artistic, and back then I kept busy with my creative interests and hobbies: writing spec screenplays, video editing, learning full stack JavaScript, and making lots of vector illustrations.

The beloved and pampered Scribbles (2003–2014) is our late chihuahua, who often took sides in her mother and fathers disputes when she wasn’t succumbing to sleeping or running around excitedly in small circles.

About the Making Of:

Hardly Funny showcases the comical and absurd outcomes of day-to-day situations when living with a programmer. I began documenting the unusual acts and behavior of unusual Randall soon after living together as husband and wife. The idea for the webcomic was born when others simply laughed at our tribulations. It stayed an idea for quite some time until summer 2012. From then until early 2014, I illustrated and posted Hardly Funny while Randall inadvertently came up with the material just by being himself.

Hardly Funny is complete. I drew 82 comics between January 2012 and January 2014, and every one of them is in the archive. No new comics are planned.

comics.title: Engineers

images.alt: Randall drives a blue car along a curving road with both arms thrown up, staring at a tall yellow construction crane, while Samantha sits beside him looking alarmed.

transcript: Randall: Look Samantha! A crane!
Samantha: Not again! Why do engineers have to be fascinated with cranes? We’re gonna crash!
comics.note_html: A childhood of erector sets produces an easily distracted engineer.

comics.title: We all can’t live entirely from our keyboards…

images.alt: Randall lies sick in bed, glaring and pulling tissues from a box, with used tissues scattered around, while Samantha sits on the edge of the bed.

transcript: Randall: This is all your fault... You got me sick because YOU talk to REAL people.

comics.title: Shopping with Randall

images.alt: Outside a store's fitting rooms, Samantha carries an armful of purple clothes while Randall, in a yellow T-shirt, waits holding his phone.

transcript: Sign: fitting rooms
Randall: Finally... I read like 20 pages of Reddit!
Samantha: You measure time by reading Reddit? Interesting.

comics.title: Technical vs. Literary Writing

images.alt: Samantha and Randall sit at a wooden table with two tablets on it; Randall holds an energy drink and grins.

transcript: Samantha: I know that I’m a good writer because people have told me so.
Randall: I know that I’m a good writer because of my conversion rates!
Caption: I don’t know what conversion rates are but he says this to me....
comics.note_html: Congrats on writing your first book honey! I’ll read all of it and understand some of it. Yay! http://www.theherokuhackersguide.com/

comics.title: Wedding Planning

images.alt: Samantha, in a pink top, throws her arms up excitedly about their wedding while Randall shrugs with his palms up and a sly smile.

transcript: Samantha: I want our wedding to be simple and fun and perfect!
Randall: How about a LAN party?!
comics.note_html: When we planned our wedding in college, Randall thought a LAN party would be the perfect setting. He said that everybody could mingle in their swivel chairs and game together. Nope!

comics.title: The hijacking of our new bookcase.

images.alt: Randall stands proudly with hands on hips beside a tall bookcase packed with his programming books, while Samantha, hands clasped, eyes it skeptically.

transcript: Randall: Pretty 1337, huh? I’ve got them organized categorically: web design, Python, Unix internals, algorithms, cryptography, databases and C!
comics.note_html: I only understand what 1337 means, and that concept took awhile to accept. :s

comics.title: When Gaming Comes Between Us

images.alt: At a couples counselor's office with a "love doctor" door sign, Samantha sits worried while Randall, in a Linux penguin T-shirt, grins at a laptop showing the Steam logo.

transcript: Sign: love doctor
Samantha: So the Mayans were right?
Counselor: I’m sorry, this may be the end for you two...
Caption: Steam for Linux: why everything will stop in 2012
comics.note_html: Steam for Linux will smother our marriage and shatter my world. I do like to game and Randall introduced me to Steam years ago. I, however, can stop gaming to do things like eat and sleep and live, whereas Randall simply cannot. Thanks to Steam finally coming out on Linux, I must strategically plan a few electricity outages to remind Randall who I am and that we have a relationship. My life got harder and his better. I see the fate of 2012 now, just when I thought we would make it.

comics.title: Exquisite Man

images.alt: Samantha, in a light blue dress, holds up Randall's new notebook and a pencil while Randall stands with one finger raised, explaining.

transcript: Samantha: Why did you buy a moleskin notebook?
Randall: So that one day it will be framed in a museum where people will admire my API sketches and say, “What an exquisite man.”
Samantha: You really want to be the Ron Burgundy of programming huh?
comics.note_html: It is very rarely that Randall lays his programming hands on an “old fashioned and outdated medium” such as paper. He often makes fun of me for even owning pencils and pens (just type everything instead, right?). However, he recently ordered this special moleskin notebook on Amazon along with an architect drafting pencil. He said they were the best and oh so special! He talked it about constantly until it finally arrived, and I asked him what he planned to do with it. If you know my husband, you know he is very motivated-or obsessive- about what he wants. He wants to be his personal best and plans to sleep when he dies. He also apparently plans to be remembered by his contributions and APIs. That’s great! The problem is, I am still wrapping my head around the definition of an API because I’ve never used one personally as a developer. While Randall is very motivating, the things he says are, yet again, unusual and entertaining at times. I do admire his ambitions, and perhaps someday I can fully appreciate his APIs.

comics.title: Defying Logic

images.alt: Randall raises his clenched hands beside his head in frustration at a jogger running in place by a traffic light, while Samantha, holding Scribbles on a leash, gestures toward the jogger.

transcript: Randall: Aahh! It’s one of those joggers again! I don’t understand!!
Samantha: What’s wrong? He’s just keeping his heart rate up until he crosses the street.
Randall: Running in place defies logic! He’s not going anywhere! Oh the inefficiency!
comics.note_html: Randall has explained to me several times that the basis of programming or telling a computer what to do, comes down to positive and negative input and output. Just like binary is clearly made up of only zeros and ones, a program’s data is objective. This objectivity is logic. Every now and then, Randall will point out something that disturbs his paradigm of logic in our reality. People who run in place are a violation of logic according to my husband’s computery mind.

comics.title: TRON

images.alt: Samantha, in a red dress and holding a bowl of popcorn, cheers in front of a TV while Randall stands behind her looking unimpressed.

transcript: Samantha: Wooohoo TRON! Go open source! Great movie!
Randall: ...Except that programs don’t have emotions, so that kind of nullifies the whole thing...
comics.note_html: Randall is lucky enough to work at home, where we work and end up watching a lot of movies. He remarked on this obvious plothole when we were watching TRON, right after we cheered for the open source resolution! We’re still fans of the film though. Just yesterday, Randall was listening to some pretty loud music with a narrator talking about being on “The Grid….in a motorcycle…”. Yup my little geek listens to the soundtrack while coding. 😀

comics.title: Energy Drinks

images.alt: Samantha throws her arms up in exasperation as Randall, knees bent, struggles to carry three stacked flats of Rockstar energy drinks.

transcript: Samantha: Why did you buy 3 flats of energy drinks?!
Randall: This is all I can carry, Samantha! I tried to get more!
comics.note_html: Programmers often assume you’re telling them to get MORE caffeine when you’re trying to tell them that they have had enough.

comics.title: Working from Home

images.alt: Seen from behind, Randall sits at his desk in heart-print boxers with his feet up, on a phone call while a cartoon plays on his laptop; energy drink cans, snacks and Scribbles in his bed surround him.

transcript: Randall: No this is a good time... I’m available. What’s up? Sure, let’s start the conference call then...

comics.title: Things Nerds Say

images.alt: Samantha, in a purple top, hugs and tickles Randall, who throws one arm in the air and yells.

transcript: Randall: STOP!! I’m begging! Tickling is against the Geneva Coventions!
comics.note_html: Who says that? Randall does. He hates being tickled–even if he laughs while he’s being tickled. He doesn’t fight back though; he just yells reasons to stop. I guess, as a developer, he is accustomed to using his mind instead of his body to solve problems, so he doesn’t physically stop me from tickling him.

comics.title: qwerty

images.alt: Samantha's hand holds up a pink anniversary card covered in scrawled, unreadable handwriting, while Randall stands nearby scratching his head.

transcript: [The card is covered in scribbled, illegible handwriting, with a clear "<3" near the bottom above an illegible signature.]
Samantha: Honey, the only thing legible in this card is a less-than symbol and a three!
Randall: That’s a heart sweetie!
comics.note_html: My husband is not used to using pencils and paper; perhaps most developers are this way. Most writing is illegible and occasionally, there are symbols or binary. In our love notes from high school, he would jot down code and it bewildered me. Now he writes hearts in all of the cards he gives me. They are written as if he typed them with a keyboard and had to resort to <3. He’s like a computer or a little WallE. At least I understand what the hearts mean!

comics.title: Funsucker

images.alt: Samantha sits smiling with a laptop, Scribbles peeking out of a cornucopia basket at her feet, while Randall stands with his hands clasped, frowning.

transcript: Samantha: OMG! A pilgrim name generator! It says you’re Cuthbert Cuthbertson!  And it says Scribbles is Cuthbert Cuthbertson too!
Randall: Sounds like those programmers forgot to seed their random number generator!
comics.note_html: If you get overexcited about holidays like me, you might make pilgrim and Native American seating place cards with specially generated names on them for everyone at your table! It’s almost fun for everyone until someone points out the flaws in the application. I ended up using a better pilgrim-name generator online that Randall is sure to approve of.

comics.title: Dropbox

images.alt: Randall happily holds up his laptop and an energy drink, while Samantha, wearing an apron and holding a spray bottle and cleaning rag, looks at him.

transcript: Randall: Ah, you know that nice feeling you get when everything is all clean and tidy? I feel like that, because I finally organized all my Dropbox files!
Samantha: Oh... I thought you noticed that I just cleaned the kitchen.
comics.note_html: Tonight my honey spent the rest of his holiday weekend cleaning out his Dropbox (cloud drive). I spent the day cooking two pies and then cleaning up the mess just as Randall declared how great it was to finally sort through like years of files and pictures online. I thought it was funny and a bit nerdy that even his “winter cleaning” is virtual. It is comforting to know he’s been using Dropbox (and Google Drive) for a long time now since free cloudsharing is so awesome!. Unfortunately, not everyone uses it yet. I’ve spent some time answering questions from curious friends and family about cloudsharing; sometimes being the wife of a developer makes you a sort of tech support or advisor. Well, I recommend you try the cloud! It is safe and private, so far, and free!

comics.title: First Impressions

images.alt: Randall excitedly points at Samantha and pumps his fist after asking her a question; a second image is a Wikipedia excerpt defining white hat and black hat hackers.
Part 2 of “First Impressions”, described in the transcript.

transcript: Randall: Are you a black hat or a white hat?!
Samantha: Black?
Randall: Yes! I knew it!
[Second image: an excerpt from Wikipedia.]
Excerpt: White hat

Excerpt: A "white hat hacker" (also known as an ethical hacker) breaks security for non-malicious reasons, perhaps to test their own personal security system, or while working for a company that needs intensive security assurance. Many hackers in this classification perform penetration tests and vulnerability assessments within a contractual agreement. Some black hat hackers will transfer over into becoming a white hat hacker after they get caught illegally breaking into a system whose company sees value in having somebody with this level of knowledge work for them.
Excerpt: Black hat

Excerpt: A "black hat hacker" (also known as a cracker) is a hacker who violates computer security with malicious intent or for personal gain. Black hat hackers form the stereotypical illegal hacking groups often portrayed in pop culture, and are "the epitome of all that the public fears in a computer criminal". Black hat hackers break into secure networks to destroy data or make the network unusable for those who are authorized to use the network. They choose their targets using a two-pronged process known as the "pre-hacking stage".
comics.note_html:
This post is dedicated to my sweet little cousin who is like a little sister to me. She was asked out by the boy she likes and she said yes! It reminded me of when Randall and I started dating about seven years ago. He would interrogate me with unusual questions like this one, “Are you a Black Hat or a White Hat?” (You can see why I found him very interesting.) Randall taught me that there are different kinds of hackers, such as black hats and white hats. Black hats hack to exploit for malicious intentions while white hats exploit to test or improve code. The good thing is doing either could get you a job after serving some jailtime. 😀

Just two kinds of hackers. Excerpt from Wikipedia. http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_hat_hacking#Black_hat

Congrats Cisa. Here’s to all the new experiences and feelings that a new relationship can bring! We’ll be black hats together if anything goes wrong!

comics.title: Handles

images.alt: Samantha sits at a laptop looking startled while Randall stands behind her clutching his head in dismay.

transcript: Randall: No! When you talk to my friends online, you have to use my handle, not my real name!
comics.note_html: Dating a developer can be lonely if you’re not a developer yourself. You may notice that there are definitely less people around, few social outings and lots of solitude and indoor time. Well, developers are not always antisocial; they just socialize online with selective humans and bots. I finally got to meet my honey’s friends online through a mystery called IRC. I was immediately lectured for referring to Randall as Randall since he preferred his alias or handle at the time (which was in leet speak!). His friends only knew his identity by his handle so I just confused everyone. I felt really bad, like I made a embarrassing impression. I’m glad everything worked out though. You learn something new everyday when you date a developer!

comics.title: A Typical Conversation

images.alt: Randall sits on the floor holding his head in frustration while Samantha lounges beside him with a drink, each talking about their own problem.

transcript: Randall: I’ve spent two days troubleshooting.....
Samantha: I think I need a hair cut.
Randall: I should’ve used memcached!
Samantha: Look at these split ends!
Randall: What are split ends?
Samantha: What’s memcached?
comics.note_html: Well, I wouldn’t call it a discussion actually. But this is an example of our daily coexisting. Sometimes it would be nice if Randall was a girl, or just almost normal. I know he wishes I was a gifted developer like him (Right now, I joke that I’m pretty good at concatenating strings and creating directories in Python). As different as we are, we find each other entertaining and intriguing. It definitely keeps things new. I get to learn about tech galore while he learns things from me, like what’s going on outside or offline. Today, I showed him how to cook chicken in the oven! I think I’ll have to spend today studying up on how exactly memcached works because I just don’t grasp the definition yet unfortunately.

comics.title: Holiday Shopping

images.alt: Samantha, in a teal dress, carries shopping bags while Randall points eagerly off toward a store.

transcript: Randall: Oooh! Can we go to Staples!? In grade school, all the cool guys and I would save up our lunch money and buy the coolest and newest mechanical pencils like Dr. Grip. Then we would trade them! They were worth more than pens because they had erasers!
Samantha: Wow, you’re so much cooler than I thought.
comics.note_html: I rarely take Randall shopping with me when I shop for myself. He usually dies inside while feigning contentment. It kills me to see him so unhappy. He recalled this pretty nerdy anecdote when we did happen to go shopping together for the holidays and had passed by an office supply store. Yup, he actually said “the cool guys” did this. I just hope they had something to eat for lunch since they weren’t spending their money on a meal. There are more interesting comics to come of other times I take Randall into the real world on shopping trips where he does and says weird things.

comics.title: The Morning News

images.alt: Randall and Samantha lie side by side in bed in the morning, each reading news on their phone; Randall smiles while Samantha looks upset.

transcript: Randall: There’s a baby pug practicing high fives on /r/Awww.
Samantha: Omg, the Syrian government might use chemical weapons!
comics.note_html: About two mornings ago, we had a candid moment while we were lazily reading the headlines in bed. I subscribe to the L.A. Times world news and Randall, to the subreddit, Awww. I was silently lamenting over the Syrian conflict and how their government may resort to using alleged chemical weapons on their own people… while Randall clamors over and exclaims an offbeat remark about this cute wittle puppy. He usually shows me a cute fuzzy wuzzy link every other morning, and I’ve come to realize that he reads these things first everyday! I have yet to catch up to his developer lifestyle. He is a dependent consumer as much as he is a faithful loyalist to his beloved Reddit and Hackernews communities– so much that if I ever use them, he finds it attractive. Nerd alert.

comics.title: Peculiarity

images.alt: Randall sits at his laptop between cans of Rockstar energy drink while Samantha, in an "I ♥ my geek" shirt, stands behind him touching his hair with a grimace.

transcript: Samantha: Ew...your hair feels crunchy.
Randall: That’s because I rotate my headphones every 30 minutes to equally distribute the pressure on my scalp.
comics.note_html: The pattern had bewildered me. Its hair was strangely dented at random times and felt crinkled. One day, it felt compelled to expose its secretive habit, and I immediately felt remorse and affection for this characteristic hermit.

comics.title: W.o.W.

images.alt: Randall looks glum as he worries about their relationship, and Samantha, in a purple dress, raises her hands and makes him an offer.

transcript: Randall: As a couple, we don’t have much in common. How are we going to have fun together?
Samantha: Okay, I’ll join a guild with you if that’s what you want.
comics.note_html: My Honeybuns and I are very different, so this concern of Randall’s comes up at times. In desperation to assure him we will always have something to enjoy together, I have offered to join a guild(World of Warcraft). I like computer games where as Randall can become ultimately consumed in them. Therefore, out of our own safety and sanity, we haven’t joined a guild yet. He says his Ubuntu operating system would also be an obstacle to accessing the game; this is the main reason I appreciate Ubuntu. 😀 I’m sure it saves marriages.

comics.title: Sassypants

images.alt: Four panels: Scribbles sits in laundry with heart-print underwear on his head, Randall stands smugly with hands on hips, a close-up shows his shorts, and Samantha closes her eyes, unamused.

transcript: Samantha: Randall! Scribbles is in your underwear!
[Scribbles sits in a pile of laundry with heart-print underwear draped over his head.]
[Panel 2]
Randall: All the best things are under my underwear...
[Panel 3]
[Close-up of Randall's shorts, with a dashed red outline of the underwear he's wearing underneath.]
[Panel 4]
Samantha: Hmph!
comics.note_html: My sassy Lovebug said that to me! What a clever little brat. Still doesn’t pick his underwear up off the floor, nope!

comics.title: Shopping

images.alt: At an Apple store with the glowing apple logo overhead, Samantha, in a purple dress, holds back a fist-shaking Randall as he lunges toward the display tables.

transcript: Randall: Stupid shiny unix rip offs! “Geniuses” my ass!
Samantha: Not again, Randall!
comics.note_html: Today we’re going out of town to do some holiday shopping for my husbands family. If there’s an Apple store at the mall, then I’ll literally have to talk Randall out of waltzing in there and quizzing the associates about the history, hardware, and sourcecode of just about anything computer related. It’s the only time he scoffs at people.

comics.title: Optimization

images.alt: Samantha, wrapped in a towel and standing on a bathroom scale, looks shocked as Randall peeks cheerfully around the door.

transcript: Samantha: Randall! Why does the scale have a picture of me with my name on it?
Randall: Don’t you love it? It uploads our BMI,fat percentage and weight to an online chart so we can keep track!
comics.note_html: I just realized there’s no point in hiding my weight from him since he can just go online and analyze it. I really should cut back on the holiday feasting.

comics.title: Church

images.alt: Samantha and Randall sit side by side in a church pew, seen from behind. Randall's thought bubble puts the Flying Spaghetti Monster over the cross at the front.

transcript: [No dialogue.]
[Randall's thought bubble shows the Flying Spaghetti Monster, a tangle of noodles with two meatballs and eyes on stalks, in front of the cross.]
comics.note_html: I’m going to church tonight with my in laws and my love, who taught me all about “his Holiness”, the Flying Spaghetti Monster. I’m sure that’s what he’ll be pondering about at tonights service.

comics.title: Raspberry Pie

images.alt: Randall stands sadly beside a Christmas tree with an empty stocking and torn wrapping paper on the floor, while Samantha, in pajamas, cheerfully offers to help.

transcript: Randall: I’m jealous. Mike got a Raspberry Pi for Christmas.
Samantha: Don’t be silly, I’ll whip one up for you sweetie!
Randall: It’s a credit-card sized programmable computer!
Samantha: ...Oh.
comics.note_html: Recently, our friend was bragging about his new raspberry pi while on the phone with Randall. Poor Randall was very jealous. I know how much he loves all kind of berries and pies, although I’ve never seen him have a slice of raspberry pie. I, relying on my wifey skills, offered to bake him one. I felt like I could solve this problem! That’s when he told me it had nothing to do with my baking potential or scope of knowledge. Apparently, a raspberry pi is a new kind of tiny programmable computer that only costs like 35$. I felt stupid because this happens when he talks about Tastypie too.

comics.title: My First Time

images.alt: In a drab office full of cubicles, Samantha sits at her desk clutching a desk phone and pleading with the person on the line.

transcript: Samantha: Wait! What’s India like? Don’t go! Please, it’s so boring here!
comics.note_html: It was exhilarating when I got to call India for the first time! Everything seemed outdated at my first internship. The official company-assigned emails were administered through Microsoft Outlook, and nobody knew what was going on or cared much about the big picture. That’s where I learned that most people hate their jobs and are miserable yet content enough. You can imagine how enthralled I was when I could call India on speed dial and they instantly listened AND helped me! My new Indian contact was halfway around the world and I knew immediately that we had the potential to be best friends! We could be spending hours and hours exchanging cultural stories! But no, my Indian guide with a computer-generated, American name wouldn’t spend anymore time with me unless it was purely for tech support. It was just like being at home with Randall when he’s focused on something. And I was alone again. Emo, I know.

comics.title: Nightmares

images.alt: Randall talks in his sleep in bed while Samantha sits up next to him, puzzled, and Scribbles lies at the foot of the bed.

transcript: Randall: Zzzzz..... No!...No...I’m not installing anymore servers... Zzzzz
[Samantha has a thought bubble with a question mark.]
comics.note_html: Randall claims that he programs in his dreams and I’ve heard that other programmers do too. I hear him mumbling commands in his sleep until he wakes up super excited to code! On the other hand, I can recall some of his bad dreams where he will yelp about zombies or installing servers. I suppose those two are equally bad. Poor thing.

comics.title: Tech Support

images.alt: Three panels of Samantha at her office desk in a pink top, on the phone with tech support and growing more exasperated.

transcript: Samantha: Soooo it took 8 seconds to return a ping?
[Panel 2]
Samantha: And just to clarify, you’re saying that’s normal?
[Panel 3]
Samantha: Thanks a lot.
comics.note_html: I learned all about pings when I first took a networking class in high school to be near my then-crush (now husband). I like to show off that I know what a ping is but it doesn’t necessarily help in certain situations…. like when the internet crapped out at work and tech support said it was fine.

comics.title: New Year Resolutions

images.alt: Randall excitedly tells an unimpressed Samantha about a friend's beard. By the last panel both have heart eyes, picturing a glowing bearded figure on a hill above tiny worshippers.

transcript: Randall: My friend Alven’s going to grow his beard out for a whole year!
Samantha: So?
[Panel 2]
Randall: A beard like that on a developer is like having the golden fleece on your face!
Randall: It will have powers!
[Panel 3]
Randall and Samantha: Oooohh...
[Their shared thought bubble shows a radiant man with a huge white beard standing on a hill above tiny cheering stick figures.]
comics.note_html: Our friend has natural Billy Mays-like powers for beard growing and he mentioned that he is under some playful pressure to grow it out. Randall has burst with beard envy twice now. The beard will need a name.

comics.title: Girl Talk

images.alt: Samantha, in a green dress, has lunch at a small café table with a woman friend in a yellow sweater and jeans. The two are comparing their husbands' complaints.

transcript: Samantha: My husband always complains about people not putting sufficient comments in their code.
Friend: ....Interesting. My husband complains when his patients don’t brush their 2nd bicuspids. He’s a dentist.
comics.note_html: I thought it was pretty funny when my coworker could recall the formal names of teeth just because her husband talks about them all the time. It’s entertaining what we pick up from our family members and their lines of work.

comics.title: Oh Facebook

images.alt: Randall stands dejected while Samantha, in a white top and green skirt, holds Scribbles in her arms and answers him.

transcript: Randall: I posted on Facebook that I finished my book and nobody said anything. Then I put a picture of you and Scribbles on there and everyone liked it!
Samantha: Don’t hate me ‘cause I’m beautiful!
comics.note_html: Sorry babe. That’s life. Most people identify with Scribbles the Chihuahua more than PaaS. I sure do!

comics.title: Why you should leave your developer at home

images.alt: At a paint-your-own-ceramics studio, Samantha paints a crane on a blue vase while Randall, in a 1337 shirt, paints a tile. A blonde staff member in an apron comes over to their table.

transcript: Samantha: This is the best date ever! I love Paint-Your-Own Ceramic!
Randall: Yup.
[Panel 2]
Samantha: I’m painting a magical crane! Me looves it!
Randall: I’m painting hexadecimal!
[Randall's tile reads: \x48\x61\x69\x6C \x53\x61\x74\x61\x6E]
[Panel 3]
Staff member: Aw, what a cute couple! What do all those numbers mean, young man?
Randall: It’s hexadecimal for Hail Satan.
[Samantha looks horrified.]
comics.note_html: Now we have a personalized-by-Randall ceramic candle holder that reads Hail Satan in hexadecimal. Not good. Not good at all. I regret taking Randall there but it’s my favorite place and I’m counting down until our next visit on Valentines Day!

comics.title: Parents of Programmers

images.alt: Two mothers, one in purple and one in cream, brag about their sons' computer books. Below, they admit they're lost as a man in a teal shirt and tie points upward to explain.

transcript: Mom in purple: My son wrote a book. It’s about computers!
Mom in cream: So did my son!
[Panel 2]
Mom in purple: I don’t understand it though.
Mom in cream: Me neither.
Dad: Heroku is a type of karate, Honey!
comics.note_html: I believe Randalls dad actually said he should “open up a can of Heroku” if anybody gives him a hard time.

comics.title: Randall’s Grand Idea

images.alt: Randall proudly points to a calculator in his hand as Samantha, in a purple top and jeans, stares back at him in dismay.

transcript: Randall: According to my calculations, we only need $2.7 million dollars to live off $40,000 a year at a 2% interest rate!
Samantha: We need $2.7 million!
comics.note_html: Randall determined this equation after we both started working our first jobs and hated it. I don’t know if we’ll ever attain an account balance of $2.7 million dollars while there’s a still a bank that offers a 2% interest rate. However, the idea makes him happy and hopeful, and that is priceless.

comics.title: Even with Music

images.alt: Randall walks Scribbles on a leash and grins, while Samantha, in a teal top and skirt, clutches her head.

transcript: Randall: I found the best music to program to!
Samantha: That’s soo nerdy!
comics.note_html: Randall has special music for programming. I guess it isn’t that nerdy, considering that people have music for working out to or music for romance. It just sounded so nerdy when he told me about it.

comics.title: ab Command

images.alt: Randall sits at his laptop between cans of Rockstar energy drink, fists raised and yelling in frustration.

transcript: Randall: Damn! One 'ab' command and I'm locked out of my new web service!
comics.note_html: So I don’t personally, fully understand this command, however another weird situation has happened in my life of living with a programmer. Randall exclaimed at the computer again. His friend messaged me online to let me know what kind of trouble Randall was in. It turns out my husband, Randall, accidentally locked himself out of his own application by typing the wrong command. Thanks to Craig for letting me know(uh, Randall says that you distracted him and it’s your fault he ran this command!). 😀

comics.title: StartupVitamins Posters

images.alt: Randall shows Samantha the new motivational posters in his home office. Later, she finds him hunched over his laptop.

transcript: [Posters on the wall read “HAVE PASSION” and “COMMIT 100%” (partly hidden behind Samantha).]
Randall: I got motivational posters for my office, Sweetie!
Samantha: Oooh. I’ll leave you alone so that you can be “motivated” and focus!
[Panel 2]
[Night falls outside the window as Randall sits hunched over his laptop.]
[Panel 3]
[Daytime again.]
Samantha: You’ve been gaming this whole time!?
Randall: It’s tower defense!
comics.note_html: Yup. Randall got some snazzy posters for his home office and the first thing he did while being surrounded by pure positivity, was play tower defense for three days! So….the posters definitely work. If you get any of these Startup Vitamins, as they’re called, be sure to have enough willpower to use them for good.

comics.title: The Bug

images.alt: Randall lies sprawled on the floor next to an open book while Samantha, in a pink dress, kneels beside him with her hand on her forehead.

transcript: Samantha: OMG! What happened!? Do you have food poisoning?
Randall: Samantha....HELP... The ending was so sad. I can’t move.
Samantha: Were you reading this? This isn’t a technical book... It’s a novel! Randall! You’re having something called an emotional reaction.
Randall: I’m never reading fiction again.
comics.note_html: When Randall read The Bug by Ellen Ullman, he withdrew himself and complained of how sad he felt in response to the story. I knew it was the first time (in a long time) that he had read fiction and I assumed it must’ve been a good book! I’ve heard that the protagonist is a programmer in the 1980’s, and the bug is actually referring to a bug in code. I don’t want to attempt to summarize it any further, because I haven’t read it yet. I can say that Randall does recommend it, despite his reaction.

comics.title: First Repository

images.alt: Randall, beaming, sweeps Samantha, in a purple dress, into a big hug and lifts her off her feet.

transcript: Randall: You signed up for Github!
comics.note_html: Randall went ooh la la over me when I made my first Github account and repository this week! I will use it for my new static html site that I plan to host through Amazon Web Services.

images.alt: Randall, in a black T-shirt and grey shorts, strokes his chin thoughtfully and asks a question about dinosaurs, while Samantha, in a purple dress, stands beside him and whispers behind her hand.

transcript: Randall: Do you think t-rexs slept with their heads up against cliffs so that they could rest?
Samantha: ...nerd alert!
comics.note_html: We love dinosaurs, but sometimes we have to call each other nerds.

comics.title: Time Machine

images.alt: Randall grips the wheel of a small blue car, looking panicked as he shouts, while Samantha throws her arms up in alarm in the passenger seat.

transcript: Randall: We have to get to 88 miles per hour!
Samantha: Why?!
comics.note_html: Randall speeds sometimes and tells me we just have to get to 88 mph. It took me a few years to realize that this is because he pretends he’s in the movie, Back to the Future. He wasn’t proud that it took me so long to understand. Now, we speed if there’s a van behind us because it means that “the Libyans are coming.”

comics.title: The Essentials

images.alt: Samantha, carrying a purse, walks into a new home full of unopened moving boxes. Randall sits at a desk with only his laptop, a toilet paper roll and a glass set up, and Scribbles sits under the desk.

transcript: Samantha: Why is everything still in boxes?
Randall: I unpacked everything we need.
comics.note_html: We are moving again in three weeks to San Francisco/East Bay area to attend fellow hackathons and such. The last two times that we moved, I worked full time and left the unpacking to Randall. It turned out like this image above each time; he only unpacked his laptop and some books on hacking. That was it! He didn’t see the problem, just “the essentials”.

comics.title: Being Thoughtful

images.alt: Randall hugs Samantha from behind and nuzzles her while holding out a black laptop in front of her. Samantha looks sideways, unsure.

transcript: Randall: I love you so much that I'm going to give you my old laptop so that you can finally learn UNIX!
Samantha: I guess this means that we're taking our relationship to the next level!
comics.note_html: I guess I’ll be learning UNIX. I knew it was coming to this, because he tries to reformat my computer with different operating systems when I’m not home. I’m sure UNIX is great. I just didn’t know that we were ready to take this step together. Gulp.

comics.title: Updates

images.alt: Samantha sets plates of food on a candlelit dinner table, but Randall is walking away from it, carrying his own plate and a candle.

transcript: Samantha: Honey, I made us a candlelit dinner!
Randall: Nope! There's a new OS update, and I have to try it before anyone else does!
comics.note_html: Randall loves updates (and watching progress bars load). He reformats for each OS update, which can take hours!

comics.title: Embarrassing

images.alt: At a store checkout, a cashier turns his monitor to show a screen of error text. Randall, in an "rtfm" T-shirt, gleefully points at it, while Samantha, holding a shopping basket, looks embarrassed.

transcript: Cashier: I apologize. Our computers are down. I won't be able to ring you up today.
Randall: HAH! Your kernal updates messed up the NIC drivers!!
comics.note_html: When we go out, there is occasionally a downed computer. It always serves Randall an opportunity to interpret the code and have a ball with it.

comics.title: Breaking the Cycle

images.alt: Randall lies sprawled on the floor with X's for eyes as if dead. Samantha stands over him with a hand on her hip, and Scribbles lies on the floor nearby.

transcript: Randall: Ugh, I'm out of caffeine, and I can't get up to buy more!
Samantha: So, this is the END of you?
Randall: Essentially....yes.
comics.note_html: This is why we pay Amazon Prime to deliver an almost steady supply of caffeinated drinks to our door.

comics.title: Screen of What?!

images.alt: Samantha sits at her pink desk, where her monitor shows a blue error screen. Randall stands beside it, arms flung wide, screaming in horror.

transcript: Samantha: Hey babe, can you fix my computer?
Randall: Oh my god! It's the blue screen OF DEATH!!!
comics.note_html: I didn’t know about the Blue Screen of Death until it appeared on my computer, and my husband had this reaction. This famous crash message even has a Wikipedia page with a slideshow of public sightings. How nerdy!

comics.title: 1337 Dreams

images.alt: Randall and Samantha lie in bed under a teal blanket. Randall rests with his hands behind his head, looking pleased, while Samantha looks over at him.

transcript: Randall: So while I was sleeping last night, I thought of the chapter titles for my new tech book!
Samantha: You dream of that stuff?
comics.note_html: My husband doesn’t always code in his best dreams… He designs things, like ebooks or rest APIs. I get to hear all about it in the morning! I fill him in on my dreams- usually something about me and our chihuahua, Scribbles.

comics.title: Working from Home

images.alt: Four panels: Samantha repeatedly checks on Randall, who sits in a green desk chair wearing headphones, his screen showing anime while he says he is working.

transcript: [Panel 1]
Samantha: How come whenever you're "working", you're actually watching anime?
Randall: Honey, I'm just waiting for my code to compile!
[Panel 2]
Samantha: It's been an hour, and you're still watching cartoons!
Randall: I'm waiting for my script to upload. It takes time...
[Panel 3]
Samantha: Hey you're still watching ANIME!
Randall: I'm taking a break, what do you expect?
[Panel 4]
Samantha: What about now?
Randall: I'm waiting for my data to populate!
comics.note_html: I’ve gotten used to having a husband who’s always online, but I’m not used to seeing him watch cartoons all day long. The sad thing is, I’ve come to accept that it means he’s working. I don’t know how exactly–how does one code while reading subtitles at the same time? It’s just a weird trait of a developer husband that is unexplainable and therefore hardly funny to me.

comics.title: Things Randall Says…

images.alt: While shopping, Samantha tries on a green floppy hat with a price tag. Randall, beside her, pumps his fists excitedly.

transcript: Samantha: Will you buy me this hat?
Randall: You look like Link from Zelda! Of course I'll get it for you!
Samantha: I don't know who that is but okay!
comics.note_html: My honey said this when we went shopping and I found this cutesy green hat! I’ve only played Zelda once, but I found a picture of this character, Link online. Now I know!

comics.title: Making Conversation

images.alt: Samantha stands by Randall's desk and asks a question as he leans back in his chair with his legs stretched out and crossed, typing on a laptop.

transcript: Samantha: How's Cora?
Randall: Cora was my old computer! This one is named Death, and he's doing just fine.
comics.note_html: I try to make conversation with my busy programmer husband by asking how his computer is doing. I forgot he got a new computer a while ago and that I hadn’t learned the name of it yet. Whoops! It’s not easy to get used to the fact that he names computers, let alone remembering their names! Well, this one is called Death, and it lives with us. I didn’t like Cora because Randall spent all his time with her. Death’s been okay so far.

comics.title: Quality Time

images.alt: Randall sits smiling behind an open Newegg box, while Samantha sits on the floor with her arms reaching deep inside a computer tower case, looking unhappy. Parts and cables lie around them.

transcript: Randall: Wow! We should build computers together more often... your fingers are the perfect size!
comics.note_html: Randall and I built my desktop together. It was the first computer and only computer that I’ve built. We picked out all the parts from Newegg.com and built it for like 500 bucks. I think that was about four or five years ago. I still use it. After we built it, I got to learn about drivers and opensource software. We had to find all the applications and the operating system online to download and install. It was a totally new experience and a bargain. Randall said my small fingers saved him hours of struggle too! (We would do it more often but have since happened to buy only laptops.)

comics.title: Moving

images.alt: Samantha holds a phone and reads off her apartment search, while Randall, holding a laptop and a water bottle, stands beside her.

transcript: Samantha: Ok... I've got all the potential apartments listed by square footage and cost....
Randall: The only thing that matters is the internet service provider!
comics.note_html: I’ve learned that the internet service provider is the most important amenity when choosing a home. In Los Angeles, we couldn’t find fiber anywhere that we had lived but now that we’re moving to Walnut Creek/East Bay, I think there is hope for a home sweet home.

comics.title: Waza

images.alt: Two panels at a party: a man in a white T-shirt talks to Samantha, both holding red cups, and points out another man in a purple shirt across the room.

transcript: [Panel 1]
Samantha: I've never been to a Github sponsored party before...
Partygoer: Welcome. That guy over there is Kenneth Reitz, and he's a sex symbol.
[Panel 2]
Samantha: Ooohh!
Partygoer: Mm hmm. He got contacts instead of glasses.
comics.note_html: So this happened at Waza and everyone wanted a comic about Waza. I don’t know who said it to me and there was a lot of free drinks being consumed but it happened. Good times.

comics.title: Favorite Number

images.alt: Two panels: Randall, hands on hips, asks Samantha a question and she answers happily with her eyes closed. In the second panel he looks unimpressed and she glares back.

transcript: [Panel 1]
Randall: What's your favorite number?
Samantha: 31!
[Panel 2]
Randall: That's so typical. You'd choose a whole number.
comics.note_html: That little bratty programmer husband of mine said this to me! And then he went on and on about Pi and how amazing it is. That will be the next comic…

comics.title: Hacker Wardrobe

images.alt: Photo of a closet shelf with three tall stacks of folded T-shirts: printed tech shirts, plain white shirts, and plain black shirts, with a water bottle in front.

transcript: Caption: A Hacker's Wardrobe:
[Labels with arrows under each stack, left to right:]
Label: Tech shirts
Label: White shirts
Label: Black shirts
comics.note_html: So we just moved and I unpacked my husband’s clothes for him (because I’m amazing). It was pretty easy considering he only owns a few essential hacker necessities. He has tons of tech shirts but usually opts for a black t-shirt. In fact, ever since we started dating, I told him that he reminds me of a cartoon character because he wears the same thing all the time. I like that he values comfort and simplicity but he needs to at least start dressing up for Halloween.

comics.title: A Pen?

images.alt: A leasing agent points to a document on a table. Samantha sits across from them, and Randall stands behind her, staring at the pen in his hand.

transcript: Leasing agent: Sign your new lease in black pen on the dotted line...
Randall: I haven't used one of these in years!
comics.note_html: My hacker husband has awful handwriting. It looks like someone dipped a chicken’s feet in ink and let them scurry all over a poor sheet of paper. But how fast can he type you ask? Incredibly fast! He is a ninja with the keyboard yet defeated with the old-fashioned paper and pen. When we signed our last lease, he said this quote above out loud and I found it quite embarrassing.

comics.title: Precious Heartbeats

images.alt: Two panels: Samantha asks Randall about going running. Below, she stands with hands on her hips, indignant, while Randall shrugs with palms up.

transcript: [Panel 1]
Samantha: How come you never go running with me?
Randall: The typical mammalian heart usually stops after two billion beats, so I try to avoid cardio at all costs.
[Panel 2]
Samantha: And you never told me?!
comics.note_html: I’ve done some research after rudely finding out Randall was watching me use up my limited amount of heartbeats….I found that most sources say mammal and human hearts will beat between 2 and 3 billion times. That’s a pretty big discrepancy, but it depends on how long the person lives. The worldwide average life expectancy is supposedly 65 years old (2 billion beats), but I might be lucky enough to reach 95 years of age (3 billion beats). All in all, doing cardio regularly actually slows your sitting heart rate and therefore helps you out in the long run. Hah! (I made a pun.) So Randall started running with me!

comics.title: Happy Birthday to Me!

images.alt: Samantha sits on the floor holding a small game box, looking dismayed, next to an opened pink gift box. Randall sits across from her, gesturing at the gift.

transcript: Samantha: You got me Warcraft for my birthday?
Randall: What's wrong?
comics.note_html: Today is my birthday(and Easter)! I just remembered it’s my twin sister’s birthday too, so happy birthday Allison! Anyway, one year Randall gave me Warcraft ( in a little software box-remember those?) as a present. I was livid. First of all, I hadn’t played the game in years! Secondly, it cost money to play! That turned into a fight… especially when I found out he threw out the receipt. Oh well, it was still nice of him.

comics.title: Date Night

images.alt: Randall and Samantha at a candlelit anniversary dinner over spaghetti, with a "3 years" heart card on the table. Randall gestures mid-lecture while Samantha looks glazed over.

transcript: Randall: So that’s pretty much what a content delivery network is.
Samantha: Oh. Well, happy anniversary honey!
[A card on the table reads: 3 years]
comics.note_html: Happy Anniversary Baby! Congrats on three years of marriage. It doesn’t feel like forever yet, so that’s a good sign!

comics.title: Angry Randall

images.alt: Randall stands with fists raised, shouting angrily, while Samantha stands beside him looking wide-eyed and impressed.

transcript: Randall: I could replace his job with a two line Bash script!
Samantha: Ooohh!
comics.note_html: It takes a lot to anger Randall, but he never fails to yell this after talking to Comcast. I just learned what Bash is the other day even though I’ve been using it for almost a year. I initially thought it was a language! Wow. Even a simple shell script can replace a job.

comics.title: Robotics!

images.alt: Randall cheers with raised fists and Samantha frowns beside him as they watch a robotics competition, where a boxy robot loaded with balls and a smaller robot roll across the arena floor.

transcript: Randall: Robots! Epic! When do they start blowing each other up?
Samantha: How many times do I have to tell you? This is not that kind of contest!
comics.note_html: We attended our first robotics competition! That’s what we do for fun now….yeah. It was a regional F.I.R.S.T. Robotics Competition at San Jose State. My geeky husband, who pirates too many violent shows, kept asking when the robots were going to destroy each other. Thankfully, they never did and instead displayed their many impressive and uber exciting skills. All the robots were built by teenagers and were sponsored by some pretty big names including NASA and Google! We’ve added robotics to our list of things to do this year as a couple. You should definitely check out some video of the competition here: Time Magazine covers FIRST.

comics.title: Ideal Hackathon

images.alt: Two panels. Randall raises a finger to pitch a meetup idea to a smiling Samantha, then throws his hands up excitedly as she stands skeptically, holding Scribbles the chihuahua on a leash.

transcript: [Panel 1]
Randall: I have an idea for a meetup...
Samantha: A DoS attackers group? Hah!
[Panel 2]
Randall: No! A hackathon with... black lights and alcohol and hacker movies playing and loud music too! No rules! No set projects! No formalities!
Samantha: Oh no.
comics.note_html: Randall’s newest evil plot: a hackathon that will probably attract black hats. Eeek! On the safer side, we are considering starting a coding group for the East Bay on Meetups.com.

comics.title: Investing

images.alt: Two panels. Samantha voices a money worry to Randall, who is seated in a green chair with a laptop. Then Randall throws his arms up triumphantly while Samantha stares, horrified.

transcript: [Panel 1]
Samantha: I’m worried that we’re not saving enough money for retirement.
Randall: Hmmm...
[Panel 2]
Randall: I spent ALL our savings on Bitcoin! You don’t have to save or worry ever again!
Samantha: Oh god!
comics.note_html: Theoretically, he’s right. We can possibly make more money than a savings account’s interest rate offers if we invest in things instead. It is always a gamble however. At least my husband is excited about getting ready for the financial future now. Randall was so excited that the next day he built a command line app to handle your personal BitCoin called BTC. Check it out here, http://rdegges.github.io/btc/.

comics.title: API Testing

images.alt: Randall lies stretched out on the floor with his laptop, clutching his face and yelling at the screen. Samantha stands over him with a hand on her hip, unimpressed, as he explains himself.

transcript: [Panel 1]
Randall: Null? Batch request denied?! NOOOOOOOOO!
[Panel 2]
Samantha: You’ve been laying here all day talking to yourself!
[Panel 3]
Randall: I’m testing my API! I have to watch it run and catch errors...
[Panel 4]
Samantha: Then you just lay there after they arise?
Randall: Yes. I’m going to fix them later. This is an important part! Trust me!
comics.note_html: Yes, my honey buns likes to lay down all the time when he’s working from home. I found out he’s actually “watching the API run” and monitoring errors. Then he looks through the data later to troubleshoot! What a long process. I can tell he likes laying down almost as much as coding APIs.

comics.title: Logic-Loving Husband

images.alt: Samantha swoons with raised arms in front of a pink heart, professing her love to Randall. He responds with a literal-minded question, leaving her facepalming and then clutching her head.

transcript: [Panel 1]
Samantha: Baby! I’m head over heels for you!
Randall: I have never understood what that means... Isn’t one’s head always over one’s heels? Why would it be something worthy of pointing out?
[Samantha facepalms.]
[Panel 2]
Samantha: ...it means I really like you!
Randall: Wha? How on earth do you get that?
comics.note_html: So programmers are programmed (like the programs that they write) to think logically and that creates a sort of, human error problem for Randall sometimes. When I told him that I was “head over heels” for him once, he was very confused as illustrated in exhibit A above. I suppose that I sound just as confusing to him too.

comics.title: Infinite Recursion

images.alt: Randall and Samantha eat tacos, then later in a grocery store Randall holds up a bag of Doritos and shouts excitedly while Samantha stands by a shopping cart looking embarrassed.

transcript: [Panel 1]
Randall: Wow! Dorito-flavored tacos!
[Panel 2]
[In a grocery store, Randall holds up a bag of Doritos with a taco pictured on it.]
Randall: Hey! These new Doritos are flavored like the taco, that’s flavored like the doritos!
Randall: It’s INFINITE RECURSION!
comics.note_html: It was really embarrassing when Randall started yelling “Infinite recursion!” in the grocery store. I didn’t know how to calm him down. I didn’t want to explain, to strangers, the excitement of his epiphany, mostly because people just won’t understand. There’s a new taco at Taco Bell, flavored like Dorito chips. After it became popular, Doritos had to continue flavoring things…. Doritos now has a new chip that is flavored after the taco that was initially flavored after themselves…. It is like a never ending loop!

comics.title: Left 4 Dead

images.alt: Samantha, sitting at her laptop, complains to Randall about an online zombie game. In the next panel Randall hugs her with a proud, contented smile while she looks glum.

transcript: [Panel 1]
Samantha: Dude! The zombie hoard was coming and my teammate died- so I used the defibrillators on him and then- he got up and killed me for no reason!
[Panel 2]
Randall: I’m just proud that you’re gaming, sweetie!
comics.note_html: Randall bought me a Steam account after we got married. I use it mostly to play Left 4 Dead, a fun, easy, zombie crazy, first person shooter game. I’m not very good at most other games on Steam. You have to get through a zombie ridden level of play with three strangers online as teammates. This requires teamwork, communication and smart decision making to ensure team survival, just like a real zombie apocalypse! Sometimes I get really into it, (you get a lot of chances to try and win), but everything can be ruined when other online gamers act stupid or fail.

comics.title: Randall Goes Outside

images.alt: Randall stares suspiciously at a field full of golden haystacks, and Samantha gestures toward them to explain.

transcript: [Panel 1]
Randall: What is this?
[Panel 2]
Randall: Is this a sick cult of people who cube weeds?
[Panel 3]
Samantha: Those are called haystacks.
Randall: Oh.
comics.note_html: My programmer of a husband said this one time as we drove past a field, while on a road trip. He doesn’t get out much, and I guess that he doesn’t see a lot of haystacks online. He’s so weird. I would know; I’m pretty weird myself.

comics.title: Houserules

images.alt: Two panels labeled "Most Couples" and "Us". In both, Randall glares over Samantha's shoulder as she uses her laptop, but for different reasons; a big "Nope!" burst ends the second panel.

transcript: Caption: Most Couples:
Randall: Hey, who’s that guy that’s poking you on facebook? That’s flirting, and you should never talk to him again.
Caption: Us:
Randall: Who’s this guy posting on your facebook in all caps? Ew! And he’s using Comic Sans?
Randall: Nope!
comics.note_html: Some things aren’t tolerated by computer programmers, such as people who type in all capitals and people who use Comic Sans font. It’s kind of like saying, “Look at me, I’m a douchebag.” It makes my Lovebug yell, “Nope!” which is something else unique about his kind….

comics.title: Slow Internet

images.alt: Randall lies sprawled on the floor with X's for eyes, a hand raised dramatically, while Samantha stands over him gesturing in exasperation.

transcript: Randall: Nooo! It’s amazing how a slow internet connection can ruin your life! Ugh! Facepalm!
Samantha: Randall! There are other things in life. And-what the hell is facepalm?
Randall: Double Facepalm!
comics.note_html: Yup, poor lovebug just dies when the internet is slow. At least it taught me what a facepalm is. I didn’t know he has to title actions now. Must be a Reddit thing.

comics.title: Potentially Perfect

images.alt: Randall excitedly tells Samantha, who is eating a banana, about another couple he met, gesturing enthusiastically as she listens with a flat expression.

transcript: [Panel 1]
Randall: I met a graphic designer that’s married to a programmer!
[Panel 2]
Randall: Don’t you see how that’s perfect?!
Randall: He codes the back end, while she designs the front end!
Samantha: Oh
comics.note_html: Another Randall epiphany moment. Maybe one day my site designing skills will be good enough for us to be potentially perfect too!

comics.title: Parking Problems

images.alt: In a parking lot, Samantha gestures indignantly at a reserved parking sign next to a row of cars while Randall looks on, then Randall grins and makes a proposal of his own.

transcript: [Panel 1]
Samantha: Expectant mother parking? You gotta be kidding me! What about energy efficient vehicles?!
[Panel 2]
Randall: What about hackers?! Seriously, we should get priority parking!
comics.note_html: I am miffed that uber pregnant people get priority parking over everybody else at certain Targets and grocery stores. And then Randall proposed that he should get the priority parking! …our first-world problems…

comics.title: Disconnected

images.alt: Samantha smiles and holds hands with Randall, but Randall looks glum and admits something about how he feels away from his computer.

transcript: [Panel 1]
Samantha: Isn’t this fun?!
Randall: Actually...
[Panel 2]
Randall: I always want to code whenever I leave my desk.
[Panel 3]
Samantha: Why?
Randall: Because everything offline sucks.
Samantha: Oh no...
comics.note_html: Poor lovebug and I went to a concert, where he said this to me. I know what he means though, especially if being offline means talking to strangers, who he calls “not programmers”.

comics.title: Testing Telephony

images.alt: Randall grins and steeples his fingers as Samantha's phone rings. She answers to a strange automated message, then angrily confronts Randall while he laughs.

transcript: [Panel 1]
Phone: Ring! ring!
[Panel 2]
Samantha: Hello?
Phone: This is yourself from the future...I want you to know--
[Panel 3]
Samantha: Randall! STOP testing your phone apps on me--or else!
Randall: Muahahaha!
comics.note_html: Evil Randall and his telephony (an actual industry) tricks. I always get random phone calls, sometimes with automated voices telling me weird things like this or just a series of beeps. I’m tired of answering my phone and being hung up on and then hearing, “Samantha! My program was able to correctly identify your voice and parse the data!” It’s so annoying when you’re a guinea pig and you don’t know it.

comics.title: Easy Reading

images.alt: Randall relaxes in a clawfoot bubble bath with candles, reading an "html 5" book, while Samantha stands beside the tub in a towel, glaring at him.

transcript: Samantha: You’re reading about HTML in your bubble bath?
Randall: It relaxes me.
[The book cover reads: html 5]
comics.note_html: So I couldn’t get into the bath the other day because Randall had cozied up with none other than “HTML 5: an Overview”. Now, whenever I read code books, which is not very often, I do it in front of a keyboard. Maybe this is why Randall takes a bazillion baths and buys a bazillion books.

comics.title: Thanksgiving

images.alt: Samantha delightedly shows Randall a pilgrim name generator on her laptop at their Thanksgiving table, and Randall's bored look turns to indignation at the result.

transcript: [Panel 1]
Samantha: Omg! A pilgrim name generator!
[Panel 2]
Randall: Oh, that will make this so much more fun.
[Panel 3]
Samantha: It says you’re Cuthbert Cuthbertson! And Scribbles is Cuthbert Cuthbertson too!
Randall: What?!
Randall: Whoever made that forgot to seed the random number generator!
comics.note_html: I made placecards for Thanksgiving and found a way to look up pilgrim names. Don’t worry realists, I made Native American ones too. Anyway, Randall was pretty upset that a not-so-passionate programmer forgot to seed his random number generator and therefore, made our names the same.

comics.title: DEFCON

images.alt: Samantha, walking Scribbles on a leash, asks Randall about his upcoming conference. As he cheerfully explains the name, she nervously clutches Scribbles.

transcript: [Panel 1]
Samantha: So....why is the conference that you’re going to called Defcon?
Randall: Oh! It’s named after a scale, that the government uses, to describe a level of threat...
[Panel 2]
Samantha: -gulp!
Randall: For example, a nuclear war would be a level of Defcon one!
Samantha: ...Oh my!
comics.note_html: So this is what my hacker husband, Randall, said to me when I asked him about the conference he was going to (last year). Yup. Pretty rogue-hackerish-sounding to me, and pretty normal – or “badass”- to him. DEFCON is an annual pro-hacking conference in the US that’s pretty well known for its often rebellious attitude. And just so I don’t get shot, I’ll clear the air by saying that “rebellious” can mean something like “rebellion via hacking in a righteous effort to create transparency”. And that’s all I know about DEFCON! I like how Scribbles looks in this comic. She’s just as cute in real life by the way.

comics.title: Randall’s Unusual Nostalgia

images.alt: Out holiday shopping, Randall spots an office supply store and gets starry-eyed. Samantha, carrying shopping bags, shoots him down, and later drives the car while he holds his head.

transcript: [Panel 1]
Randall: ooooh...
Randall: An office supply store! We have to get the newest mechanical pencils!
[Panel 2]
Samantha: No! Boring!
Randall: But Samantha, I used to save up my lunch money to afford Dr. Grip!
[Panel 3]
Randall: If we go now, I could buy all of them and finally be cool!
Samantha: Please don’t tell anyone else what your idea of cool is!
comics.note_html: I rarely take Randall shopping with me when I shop for myself. He usually dies inside while feigning contentment. It kills me to see him so unhappy. He recalled this pretty nerdy anecdote when we did happen to go shopping together for the holidays and had passed by an office supply store. Yup, he actually said “the cool guys” did this. I just hope they had something to eat for lunch since they weren’t spending their money on a meal. There are more interesting comics to come, of other times that I take Randall into the real world on shopping trips, where he does and says weird things.
